99235.q: How can you always have fresh tissues with you when you are out?
a: In a packet in your bag
Loose at the bottom of your rucksack
99235.e: A small packet keeps the tissues clean and dry. You can take it anywhere.
99235.m: Fresh tissues stay clean in their packet.

99236.q: What do some people wear to protect others when they cough?
99236.e: A face mask over the mouth and nose holds back many droplets. That way others are less likely to catch something.
99236.m: A face mask holds back droplets.

99237.q: Why should you not sneeze into your hands?
99237.e: You touch door handles and other people with your hands. That is how the germs get to others.
99237.m: Germs on your hands are quickly passed on.

99238.q: What flies out of your mouth and nose when you sneeze?
99238.e: When you sneeze, lots of tiny droplets spray out. They can contain germs.
99238.m: When you sneeze, tiny droplets fly through the air.

99239.q: What should you do when you need to cough?
a: Turn away and cough into the crook of your elbow
99239.e: You turn away from other people and cough into the crook of your elbow. That way fewer droplets reach others.
99239.m: When you cough, you turn away.

99240.q: Which illness often spreads through sneezing and coughing?
99240.e: Cold viruses are in the droplets from sneezing and coughing. That is how others catch it.

99241.q: Why do you keep your distance from people who are coughing a lot?
a: So you do not catch anything
99241.e: The droplets only fly a short distance. If you keep your distance, fewer germs reach you.
99241.m: Keeping your distance protects against infection.

99242.q: What do people in Switzerland often say when someone sneezes?
99242.e: When someone sneezes, you wish them “Gesundheit” (good health). “En Guete” is what you say before a meal.
99242.m: After a sneeze, you wish someone good health.

99243.q: Why is it better to stay at home with a fever and a cough?
a: So you do not infect others
99243.e: If you are ill, you recover faster at home. And you do not infect other children.
99243.m: If you are ill, you stay at home and protect others.

99244.q: What is a cotton bud good for, for example?
99244.e: You can use the cotton wool to paint dots of colour on paper. Cotton buds are also popular for crafts.
99244.m: You can paint dots with cotton buds.

99245.q: What is good for cleaning the outer ear when you wash?
99245.e: A damp flannel gently cleans the outer ear and behind the ear. Then you dry it well.
99245.m: You clean the outer ear with a flannel.

99246.q: Which part inside the ear can a cotton bud damage?
99246.e: The eardrum is a thin skin deep inside the ear. A cotton bud can damage it.

99247.q: Where on your ear may you use a cotton bud?
a: Only on the outside of the outer ear
99247.e: You can clean carefully on the outside of the outer ear. A cotton bud does not belong in the ear canal.
99247.m: Cotton buds are only for the outside of the ear.

99248.q: Where does a used cotton bud go?
99248.e: Cotton buds block pipes and sewage works. That is why they go in the bin.
99248.m: Cotton buds go in the bin.

99249.q: What is the tip of a cotton bud made of?
99249.e: Soft cotton wool is wrapped around the end of the stick. That is where the name comes from.
99249.m: A cotton bud has tips made of cotton wool.

99250.q: What do you do if your ear is blocked with earwax?
a: Wait a long time and say nothing
99250.e: A doctor can remove the earwax safely. Poking around in your ear yourself can hurt it.
99250.m: If your ears are blocked, the doctor can help.

99251.e: Earwax is usually yellow to brown. It is a soft, waxy substance.

99252.q: What do you wash your hair with?
99252.e: Shampoo is a liquid soap for your hair and scalp. It gets your hair clean.
99252.m: You wash your hair with shampoo.

99253.q: Do only children with unwashed hair get head lice?
a: No, it has nothing to do with dirt
99253.e: Lice climb from head to head, whether the hair is clean or not. It has nothing to do with dirt.

99254.q: Why do you close your eyes when you wash your hair?
99254.e: If shampoo gets in your eyes, it stings. With your eyes closed, that does not happen.
99254.m: Keep your eyes closed when washing your hair.

99255.q: What do you use to untangle wet hair?
99255.e: A wide-toothed comb loosens knots in your hair. You comb carefully from the bottom upwards.
99255.m: You untangle wet hair with a comb.

99256.q: What helps long hair to be combed more easily after washing?
99256.e: Conditioner makes hair soft and smooth. Then it gets fewer knots.

99257.q: Where do you massage the shampoo in well when you wash your hair?
a: On the back of your neck
99257.e: Grease and dandruff collect on the scalp. That is why you massage the shampoo in there with your fingertips.
99257.m: You massage shampoo into your scalp.

99258.q: Why should you never use a hairdryer next to a full bath?
a: You could get an electric shock
99258.e: If a hairdryer falls into the water, electricity can flow through the water. That can kill.
99258.m: Electricity and water are dangerous together.

99259.q: Why do you rinse the shampoo out well after washing?
a: So no traces stay on your scalp
99259.e: Leftover shampoo can irritate your scalp and make it itch. That is why you rinse until there is no more foam.

99260.q: How often should you change your socks?
99260.e: Your feet sweat into your socks all day. Fresh socks every day stop bad smells.
99260.m: You change your socks every day.

99261.e: Dirt, sweat and smells collect in clothes you have worn. Washing makes them clean again.

99262.q: What machine do people usually wash clothes with today?
99262.e: The washing machine washes clothes with water and washing powder. Then it spins the water out.
99262.m: Clothes are washed in the washing machine.

99263.q: What do you put on after PE?
99263.e: After sport, your PE kit is sweaty. Fresh clothes feel better and do not smell.
99263.m: After sport, you put on fresh clothes.

99264.q: What do the little pictures on a clothing label show?
99264.e: The care symbols show how warm you may wash it and whether you can iron it. That way the clothing does not get ruined.
99264.m: Care symbols tell you how to wash a piece of clothing.

99265.q: What does the number 30 in the washtub symbol on a label mean?
99265.e: The number in the washtub gives the highest washing temperature in degrees Celsius. If it is warmer, the clothing can shrink.
99265.m: The number in the washtub shows the highest washing temperature.

99266.q: Why do you not put wet clothes in the wardrobe?
99266.e: Mould grows easily in damp clothes, and they smell musty. That is why you let them dry first.
99266.m: Clothes only go into the wardrobe when dry.

99267.q: Where do you put dirty clothes?
99267.e: You collect dirty clothes in the laundry basket until they are washed. That way the clean clothes in the wardrobe stay clean.
99267.m: Dirty clothes belong in the laundry basket.

99268.q: Why do you keep your fingernails short?
99268.e: Dirt and germs get stuck under long nails. Short nails are easier to keep clean.

99269.q: What do you use to smooth rough edges on your fingernails?
99269.e: You rub the nail file gently over the edge of the nail. Then you no longer get caught on jumpers.
99269.m: A nail file smooths nail edges.

99270.q: What do you use to clean the dirt from under your fingernails?
99270.e: The small, hard nail brush gets well under the nails. With water and soap you scrub the dirt away.
99270.m: A nail brush gets your nails clean.

99271.q: Why should you not bite your fingernails?
99271.e: There are lots of germs on your fingers and under your nails. When you bite them, they go straight into your mouth.
99271.m: Nail biting puts germs in your mouth.

a: A small piece of skin sticking out at the edge of a nail
99272.e: A hangnail is a torn little piece of skin next to the nail. You cut it off carefully instead of pulling at it.
99272.m: A hangnail is a small tear in the skin by the nail.

99274.e: You collect clipped nails and throw them in the bin. That way they do not lie around.
99274.m: Clipped nails go in the bin.

99275.q: What is the right way to cut toenails?
99275.e: Toenails cut straight across do not grow into the skin so easily. Rounded corners can grow in.

99276.q: What can happen to a fingernail if you trap your finger hard?
99276.e: A bruise can form under the nail. Then the nail looks dark blue until it has grown out.
99276.m: A trapped finger can get a blue nail.

99277.q: What can you use to see bacteria?
99277.e: Bacteria are tiny and invisible to the naked eye. A microscope makes them look much bigger.
99277.m: You can only see bacteria with a microscope.

99278.q: Which food is made with the help of bacteria?
99278.e: Certain bacteria turn milk into yoghurt. The milk becomes thick and slightly sour.
99278.m: Yoghurt is made with the help of bacteria.

99279.q: Where in the body do lots of useful bacteria live?
99279.e: Countless bacteria live in the gut. They help to digest food.
99279.m: In the gut, bacteria help with digestion.

99280.q: Which medicine helps against illnesses caused by bacteria?
99280.e: Antibiotics kill bacteria or slow them down. But they do not help against viruses.

99281.e: Bacteria are living things made of just one single cell. They live almost everywhere on Earth.

99282.q: Where do bacteria especially like to multiply?
a: On hot stones in the sun
99282.e: Warmth and moisture make bacteria grow quickly. In the cold, they hardly multiply.
99282.m: Bacteria like it warm and damp.

99283.q: What can bacteria in your mouth cause if you do not brush your teeth?
99283.e: Bacteria in the mouth eat sugar and make acid. This acid attacks the teeth.
99283.m: Brushing your teeth protects against tooth decay.

99284.q: Where do used wet wipes go?
99284.e: Wet wipes do not break down in water and block the pipes. That is why you throw them in the bin.
99284.m: Wet wipes do not go down the toilet.

99285.q: What do you do after using the toilet?
99285.e: When you flush, everything goes away. Then the toilet is clean for the next person.
99285.m: Always flush after using the toilet.

99286.q: Why do you close the toilet lid before flushing?
a: So fewer splashes get into the air
99286.e: When you flush, tiny droplets splash up. A closed lid keeps them in.

99287.q: What do you often dry your hands with in a public toilet?
a: Paper towels or a hand dryer
99287.e: Public toilets have paper towels or a machine that blows warm air. That way your hands stay clean.
99287.m: In public toilets, you also dry your hands well.

99288.q: Why is it better not to take your mobile phone to the toilet?
99288.e: In the toilet, germs easily get onto your phone. Later you touch it again and hold it to your face.
99288.m: It is better to leave your phone outside when you go to the loo.

99289.q: What do you clean the toilet bowl with?
99289.e: The toilet brush stands next to the toilet. You use it to scrub dirt out of the bowl.
99289.m: The toilet brush cleans the toilet bowl.

99291.q: What do you do if the toilet roll is almost finished?
99291.e: That way the next person has enough paper too. If there is no roll, you tell an adult.
99291.m: If the paper is almost finished, you put out a new roll.

99292.q: Why do you slide down the slide by yourself?
99292.e: The Earth pulls all things towards it. This force is called gravity, and it makes you slide down the sloping slide.

99293.q: On which slide do you go faster?
a: On a very short gentle one
99293.e: The steeper the slide, the more strongly gravity pulls you along it. That is why you go faster.
99293.m: Steep slides are faster than gentle ones.

99294.q: What slows you down a little as you slide?
99294.e: When two surfaces rub against each other, it slows things down. This braking effect is called friction.

99295.q: What is the best way to brake on a slide?
99295.e: Rubber is grippy and rubs hard against the slide. That is why shoes with rubber soles brake well.
99295.m: Rubber brakes well because it is grippy.

99296.q: Why do you often slide faster on a wet slide?
99296.e: A thin film of water means you rub less against the slide. So you are slowed down less.
99296.m: Wet surfaces are often more slippery.

99297.q: Why can a metal slide be dangerous in summer?
99297.e: Metal gets very hot in strong sunshine. You can burn your skin on it, so test it with your hand first.
99297.m: Test metal in the sun with your hand first.

99298.q: Why does your hair sometimes stand on end after going down a plastic slide?
99298.e: Rubbing against plastic charges you up. Your hairs then have the same charge and push each other away.
99298.m: Rubbing against plastic can charge you up.

99299.q: Where does your speed on the slide come from?
a: From being high up at the top
From the noise of the children
From the colour of the slide
99299.e: When you climb up the ladder, you store energy by being high up. When you slide, it turns into movement.
99299.m: The higher you start, the more speed you get.

99300.q: What happens at the flat end of the slide?
a: You take off into the air
99300.e: At the flat end, gravity no longer pulls you forward. Friction slows you down until you stop.
99300.m: At the flat end the slide slows you down.

99301.q: What is an object that swings back and forth like a swing called?
99301.e: A pendulum is fixed at the top and swings back and forth. A swing is a big pendulum.

99302.q: How do you get going on a swing without being pushed?
a: Move your legs forwards and back
99302.e: If you stretch out your legs and pull them back in at the right moment, you give the swing a little energy with each swing.
99302.m: You can use your legs to get yourself going.

99303.q: Why does a swing go less and less high if nobody pushes it?
a: Air and friction slow it down
99303.e: The air and the friction at the top where it hangs slow the swing down a little. So it slowly gets smaller until it stops.
99303.m: Without a new push every swing stops.

99304.q: Where are you fastest on a swing?
a: Right at the bottom in the middle
Right at the top at the front
Right at the top at the back
99304.e: As you swing down you get faster and faster. Right at the bottom you have the greatest speed, after that you slow down again.
99304.m: A swing is fastest right at the bottom.

99305.q: Where does the swing stop for a very short moment?
99305.e: At the highest point the swing changes direction. There it stands still for a tiny moment.
99305.m: When it turns round, the swing stops briefly.

99306.q: When should you push a swing to make it go higher?
a: When it is moving away from you
When it is coming towards you
When it is hanging still and you pull
It does not matter when you push
99306.e: If you push in the same direction it is already swinging, it gets more speed. If you push against it, you slow it down.
99306.m: Always push a swing in the direction it is moving.

99307.q: Which swing swings back and forth faster?
a: The one with the biggest seat
99307.e: With a pendulum, it is mainly the length that decides how fast it swings back and forth. Short pendulums swing faster than long ones.
99307.m: Short pendulums swing faster than long ones.

99308.q: Does a heavy child on the same swing swing back and forth much more slowly than a light one?
99308.e: How fast a pendulum swings back and forth hardly depends on weight. What matters most is the length of the ropes.
99308.m: Weight hardly changes the rhythm of a swing.

99309.q: How does your body feel right at the top when the swing turns round?
99309.e: At the top, where it turns round, the seat hardly presses on you. That is why you feel very light for a moment and get butterflies in your tummy.
99309.m: At the top of a swing you feel light for a moment.

99310.q: In which direction are you pushed on a fast-spinning roundabout?
99310.e: Your body wants to keep flying straight on, but the roundabout steers you in a circle. That is why you feel a pull towards the edge.
99310.m: On a roundabout you are pulled towards the edge.

99311.q: Where on the roundabout are you moving fastest?
a: Halfway between the middle and the edge
99311.e: In one turn you travel a much bigger circle on the outside than on the inside. You have the same amount of time for it, so you are fastest on the outside.
99311.m: On the outside you spin fastest.

99312.q: Where on the spinning roundabout do you need to hold on least?
99312.e: In the middle you only turn around yourself and are hardly pulled outwards.
99312.m: The middle of the roundabout is the calmest place.

99313.q: Why do you feel dizzy after riding on a roundabout?
a: Your organ of balance is muddled
99313.e: In the inner ear there is an organ of balance with fluid in it. After spinning, the fluid keeps moving, so everything seems to spin.
99313.m: The organ of balance is in the ear.

99314.q: What does a roundabout need to start turning?
99314.e: Something that is standing still only moves when a force acts on it. On a playground roundabout, that is your push.

99315.q: What does a roundabout turn around?
a: The next piece of play equipment
99315.e: In the middle there is a fixed pole or bearing. The whole roundabout turns around it.
99315.m: A roundabout turns around its axle.

99316.q: What is the force you feel pulling you outwards on the roundabout called?
99316.e: Anyone moving in a circle feels a pull outwards. This is called centrifugal force.
99316.m: In a circle you feel centrifugal force.

99317.q: When is it safest to get off the roundabout?
a: When it is at its fastest
In the middle of a turn
99317.e: If you jump off a spinning roundabout, you take its speed with you and can fall. That is why you wait until it stops.
99317.m: Only get off when the roundabout has stopped.

99318.q: What does the mat of a trampoline do when you land on it?
99318.e: The mat gives way and is stretched downwards. Then it pulls back together and throws you up.
99318.m: A trampoline stores your energy and gives it back.

99319.q: What is attached around the edge of a trampoline between the mat and the frame?
99319.e: All the way round, many steel springs connect the mat to the frame. They stretch when you jump.
99319.m: Lots of springs hold the trampoline mat.

99320.q: Why does a garden trampoline often have a net all round it?
a: So that no rain falls in
99320.e: When jumping you can easily drift to the side. The net catches you before you fall onto the hard ground.

99321.q: How do you jump higher on a trampoline?
a: Bend your knees and push off hard
99321.e: If you bend your knees and push off hard, you press the mat down further. So it bounces you higher.
99321.m: Press the mat down further and you jump higher.

99322.q: Why is it dangerous if lots of children jump at the same time?
a: They can crash into each other
99322.e: Several jumpers disturb each other and easily bump together. That is why it is best to jump one at a time.
99322.m: On a trampoline it is best to jump alone.

99323.q: What do you call a material that goes back to its shape after being stretched?
99323.e: Elastic things such as rubber or a trampoline mat can be stretched. Afterwards they go back to their old shape.
99323.m: Elastic things spring back into shape.

99324.q: What covers the springs on a trampoline so that nobody gets hurt?
99324.e: There is a padded edge over the springs and the frame. If you land there, you do not get caught in the springs.
99324.m: The edge pad protects you from the springs.

99325.q: Where is it safest to jump on a trampoline?
99325.e: In the middle the mat bounces most evenly and you are far away from the hard frame.
99325.m: Jump in the middle of the trampoline.

99326.q: Why is it better to jump on a trampoline without shoes?
99326.e: Hard soles and little stones in the tread can wear the mat. Also, with shoes on you can hurt others more easily.
99326.m: Go on the trampoline without shoes.

99327.q: What is the place in the middle that the seesaw moves around called?
99327.e: The seesaw rests in the middle and tips around this place. It is called the pivot.
99327.m: A seesaw tips around its pivot.

99328.q: Why do many seesaws have a handle in front of the seat?
a: To hold on to when it bumps
99328.e: When the seesaw hits the bottom or reaches the top, there is a jolt. With the handle you hold on and do not fall off.
99328.m: Always hold the handle on a seesaw.

99329.q: Two children of the same weight sit equally far out. What happens?
a: One side hits the ground at once
99329.e: Both push down equally hard and equally far from the pivot. That is why the seesaw stays balanced.
99329.m: Equal weights at equal distances balance each other.

99330.q: How do you get back up on a seesaw?
99330.e: If you push off hard from the ground with your legs, your side rises. The other side then goes down.
99330.m: On a seesaw you push yourself up with your legs.

99331.q: Why is there often a piece of rubber or a car tyre under the ends of a seesaw?
a: So that the bump is soft
So that the seesaw goes faster
So that it looks more colourful
So that it does not get wet
99331.e: Without padding the seesaw would hit the ground hard. The rubber cushions the bump and protects your back.
99331.m: A rubber buffer makes the bump softer.

99332.q: What does the other side of the seesaw do when your side goes down?
99332.e: A seesaw is a straight beam with a pivot. If one end goes down, the other has to go up.
99332.m: On a seesaw one side always goes up and the other down.

99333.q: Why do you feel a jolt when your side of the seesaw hits the ground?
99333.e: You are moving down fast. When it hits the ground you are stopped very suddenly, and you feel that as a jolt.
99333.m: Stopping suddenly feels like a jolt.

99334.q: How can two small children lift an adult on a seesaw?
a: By sitting together right at the end
By sitting together in the middle
By sitting on the adult's side
By sitting apart on both sides
99334.e: Two children together are heavier than one. Right at the end of the long arm they also have the greatest leverage.
99334.m: Far out on a seesaw your weight has more effect.

99335.q: What happens if one child suddenly jumps off the seesaw while the other is up in the air?
a: The other one comes down hard
The other one flies even higher
The seesaw breaks in the middle
99335.e: Without a counterweight the seesaw tips straight down on the heavy side. The child at the top then hits the ground hard.
99335.m: Only get off once you have agreed it with each other.

99336.q: Why do you need a lot of strength in your arms when climbing?
99336.e: When you climb up, you lift your whole body. Your arms and legs work hard to do this.
99336.m: When climbing you lift your own weight.

99337.q: Why is there sand, gravel or bark chippings under a climbing frame?
a: So that a fall is softer
So that it is not dusty
99337.e: Soft ground gives way when someone falls. So you get hurt less than on tarmac.
99337.m: Soft ground protects you in a fall.

99338.q: At least how many hands and feet should be holding on when you climb?
99338.e: This is called the three-point rule: only one hand or foot moves, the other three hold on.
99338.m: When climbing, three points always hold on.

99339.q: Why are climbing frames often built from triangles?
99339.e: A triangle made of solid bars cannot be pushed out of shape without bending a bar. That makes frames especially stable.

99340.q: What should you take off before climbing in the playground?
99340.e: A bike helmet can get caught in bars or nets. Then the chin strap can become dangerous around your neck.
99340.m: Take off your bike helmet in the playground.

99341.q: Why should no cords hang down from your jacket when you climb?
99341.e: Loose cords and strings can get caught on bars or nets. That can be dangerous if you slip.
99341.m: Put loose strings away when climbing.

99342.q: What is the best way to land when you jump down from the frame?
99342.e: If you bend your knees when you land, your impact is slowed down more gently. That protects your joints and bones.
99342.m: Bend your knees when you land.

99343.q: Why does a big climbing frame not tip over when lots of children climb on it?
a: It is firmly anchored in the ground
It is tied to a tree with ropes
It is filled with air inside
99343.e: The posts go deep into the ground, often into concrete. That way the frame cannot tip over.
99343.m: Solid foundations keep play equipment safe.

99344.q: What does the seat of a zip line hang from on the cable?
99344.e: At the top of the seat there is a trolley with pulleys. The pulleys run along the tight cable.
99344.m: On a zip line a trolley rolls along the cable.

99345.q: Why do you start moving on the zip line by yourself?
a: The start is higher than the finish
The wind always blows that way
99345.e: The cable is fixed higher at the start than at the end. So gravity makes you roll down.
99345.m: A zip line slopes down from start to finish.

99346.q: Why does a zip line have pulleys instead of a simple hook?
99346.e: A hook would scrape along the cable and brake hard. Pulleys turn and glide with almost no resistance.
99346.m: Pulleys glide more easily than scraping hooks.

99347.q: What is often built in at the end of a zip line to slow you down?
99347.e: At the end the trolley bumps against a buffer with a spring or rubber. It softly absorbs the bump.
99347.m: A buffer brakes the zip line at the end.

99348.q: Why does the cable sag when a child rides on it?
99348.e: Your weight pulls down on the cable. Even a tightly stretched cable gives a little.
99348.m: Weight makes every cable sag a little.

99349.q: What should you do before you set off on the zip line?
a: Check that the way is clear
99349.e: If someone is in the way, there can be a nasty crash. That is why you only go when the way is clear.
99349.m: Only set off when the way is clear.

99350.q: What happens to you when the trolley suddenly stops at the end?
99350.e: Your body wants to keep moving, even when the trolley stops. That is why you swing forwards. This is called inertia.
99350.m: Your body wants to keep going when something brakes suddenly.

99351.q: What is the cable of a zip line usually made of?
99351.e: A steel cable is very strong and hardly stretches. It carries even heavy children safely.

99352.q: Why can you build better with wet sand than with dry sand?
99352.e: Little water bridges form between the grains. They hold the grains together, so the sandcastle stays up.
99352.m: A little water holds sand together.

99353.q: What forms when you let dry sand trickle onto a pile?
99353.e: Dry sand slides down the sides until the pile has a certain slope. That makes a cone.

99354.q: Why does water soak into sand so quickly?
a: There are gaps between the grains
99354.e: Grains of sand do not lie completely tightly together. The water runs away downwards through the many small gaps.
99354.m: Water flows through the gaps in sand.

99355.q: What happens to a sandcastle when it dries in the sun?
a: It gets as hard as stone
99355.e: The sun makes the water evaporate. Without water, the grains no longer hold together well.
99355.m: When sand dries, the castle falls apart.

99356.q: What do you use to separate fine sand from small stones?
99356.e: The sieve has small holes. The fine sand falls through, and the bigger stones stay behind.
99356.m: A sieve separates small things from big ones.

99357.q: Why do your feet sink into sand but not into tarmac?
a: The grains of sand move out of the way
99357.e: Grains of sand are loose and push aside under your weight. Tarmac is firmly joined together and does not give way.
99357.m: Loose grains give way under weight.

99358.q: Why can you pour dry sand almost like water?
a: The grains roll past each other
99358.e: The many little grains tumble over each other. That is why dry sand trickles, for example in an hourglass.
99358.m: Dry sand trickles like a liquid.

99359.q: Why does a suspension bridge wobble when you walk across it?
99359.e: A suspension bridge is not supported from below but hangs from ropes. That is why it can swing easily.
99359.m: Suspension bridges hang from ropes and swing easily.

99360.q: What happens if several children jump in time on the suspension bridge?
99360.e: Every jump in the right rhythm gives the bridge new energy, like pushing a swing. So the swinging gets bigger and bigger.
99360.m: Jumping in time makes a bridge swing harder.

99361.q: Where does a suspension bridge sag lowest?
99361.e: The ropes are fixed at the ends. In between they sag, most of all in the middle.
99361.m: The middle of a suspension bridge sags lowest.

99362.q: What is the calmest way to cross a wobbly suspension bridge?
99362.e: Calm, steady steps hardly make the bridge swing. Jumping and running make it rock.

99363.q: In which canton is the Charles Kuonen Suspension Bridge, which is almost 500 metres long?
99363.e: The Charles Kuonen Suspension Bridge near Randa in Valais is 494 metres long. It was opened for hikers in 2017.
99363.m: The Charles Kuonen Suspension Bridge is in Valais.

99364.q: What holds a suspension bridge in place at both ends?
99364.e: The ropes are anchored at both ends in solid posts or in the rock. These carry the whole load.

99365.q: Why does a suspension bridge in the playground often have nets or ropes at the sides?
a: So that you can hold on
So that birds can sit on it
99365.e: Because the bridge wobbles, you can easily lose your balance. Ropes at the sides give you something to hold and prevent falls.
99365.m: Side ropes give you a hold on suspension bridges.

99366.q: What do the ropes of a suspension bridge carry?
a: The weight of the bridge and the people
99366.e: The planks hang from the ropes. That is why the ropes carry the whole weight of the bridge and everyone crossing it.
99366.m: The ropes carry the whole suspension bridge.

99367.q: What happens if you move towards the middle of the spinning disc?
99367.e: If the weight moves closer to the middle, everything spins faster. Figure skaters use this when they pull their arms in.
99367.m: Moving weight to the middle makes a spin faster.

99368.q: Where is it easiest to push a spinning disc?
99368.e: At the edge you have a long lever to the axle. That is why you need less force there than near the middle.
99368.m: A spinning disc is easier to turn from the edge.

99369.q: Why does a well-oiled spinning disc keep turning for longer?
99369.e: Oil in the bearing lets the parts slide past each other more easily. The disc is slowed down less.

99370.q: Why should you not put your feet under the edge of a spinning disc?
99370.e: There is a narrow gap between the disc and the ground. Feet can get trapped there as it turns.
99370.m: Keep your feet away from turning parts.

99371.q: On the spinning disc, you throw a ball to a child opposite you. What do you see?
a: It seems to curve off to the side
It flies straight to the child
99371.e: While the ball is flying, the other child keeps turning with the disc. So to you it looks as if the ball is curving.
99371.m: On a spinning disc, throws seem to curve.

99372.q: You are sitting on a spinning disc. What does the playground look like to you?
a: It seems to be standing still
99372.e: Because you are spinning yourself, trees and houses move past you. It looks as if the playground is spinning.
99372.m: If you are spinning, the world seems to spin.

99373.q: One child sits at the edge, one in the middle. Who turns round more times in one full turn?
a: Both the same number of times
99373.e: Both go round exactly once when the disc turns once. The child at the edge just travels a longer way.
99373.m: On a spinning disc everyone turns the same number of times.

99374.q: Why does the disc keep turning when you stop pushing?
99374.e: Something that is moving wants to keep moving. Only friction slowly brings the disc to a stop.
99374.m: Moving things keep their momentum for a while.

99375.q: What is the best way to get up a climbing pole?
a: Pull with your arms and grip with your legs
Run up it with a run-up
99375.e: Your legs grip the pole while your arms reach higher. Then your legs push you up another bit.
99375.m: On a pole, arms and legs work together.

99376.q: Why do you slide down a smooth metal pole more easily than a rough tree trunk?
99376.e: A smooth surface hardly grips skin and clothes. So there is little friction and you slide quickly.

99377.q: Why do your hands get warm when you slide down the pole fast?
a: The sun is shining on it
99377.e: When your hands rub on the pole, heat is produced. You feel this too when you rub your hands together.

99378.q: Which workers slide down a pole in some stations?
99378.e: In some fire stations, firefighters get down a floor quickly using a sliding pole. That saves time when the alarm goes.
99378.m: Firefighters sometimes use a sliding pole.

99379.q: Why is climbing a pole harder than climbing a ladder?
a: The pole is made of rubber
99379.e: On a ladder you stand on rungs. On the pole you have to hold on just by gripping and pulling.
99379.m: Without rungs, climbing is harder work.

99380.q: Why should you never touch an icy metal pole with your tongue in winter?
99380.e: Metal draws heat out of your damp tongue very quickly. The moisture freezes at once and your tongue sticks.
99380.m: Never touch icy metal with your tongue.

99381.q: Which is easier on the pole: climbing up or sliding down?
99381.e: When you slide down, gravity helps you. When you climb up, you have to work against it.

99382.q: Why do some climbers rub white powder on their hands?
a: To make their hands smell nice
99382.e: The powder is called chalk. It soaks up sweat so that the hands do not slip.

99383.q: What is under a spring rider in the playground?
99383.e: A spring rider sits on a strong steel spring that is fixed in the ground. That is why it can rock in all directions.
99383.m: A spring rider stands on a spring.

99384.q: What does the spring do when you push the spring rider forwards?
99384.e: A bent spring always pushes back towards where it started. That is how the spring rider rocks back again.
99384.m: A spring wants to go back to its shape.

99385.q: Why does a spring rider keep rocking for a moment after you get off?
99385.e: The spring still has stored energy. It swings back and forth until the movement dies down.
99385.m: Springs keep swinging until they come to rest.

99386.q: What do you hold on to on a spring rider?
99386.e: Most spring riders have handles at the front. You hold on to them when it rocks hard.
99386.m: Always hold the handles on a spring rider.

99387.q: What does the spring under a spring rider look like?
99387.e: The spring is a thick steel wire wound up like a spiral. That way it can bend well.
99387.m: A coil spring is a wound-up wire.

99388.q: With whom does the same spring rider rock back and forth faster?
99388.e: A light child is pushed back faster by the spring. That is why the spring rider rocks in a faster rhythm with them.
99388.m: The lighter the load, the faster it bounces.

99389.q: In which directions can a spring rider rock?
99389.e: The spring is round and can bend to any side. That is why the spring rider rocks forwards, backwards and sideways.
99389.m: A spring rider rocks in all directions.

99390.q: What happens when a heavier child sits on the spring rider?
a: The spring does not bend at all
The spring bends the same amount
99390.e: More weight presses harder on the spring. That is why it gives way more than with a light child.
99390.m: More weight bends a spring more.

99887.q: What does a honeybee usually do on a collecting flight?
a: It visits only one kind of flower.
It changes kind at every flower.
99887.e: On one flight, honeybees usually stick to one kind of flower. That way the pollen reaches the right plant.
99887.m: A collecting bee usually sticks to one kind of flower.

99888.q: What is another word for the fine flower dust?
99888.e: The fine dust in flowers is called pollen. It is made of lots of tiny grains.

99889.q: Which garden vegetable needs insects to form fruit?
99889.e: Pumpkin flowers are pollinated by bees and bumblebees. Only then does a pumpkin grow.

99890.q: Which creatures pollinate many flowers at night in our part of the world?
99890.e: When the bees are asleep, moths are out and about. They visit flowers and carry pollen on.

99891.q: Why do fruit growers put bee colonies in their orchards in spring?
99891.e: The bees fly from tree to tree and pollinate the blossoms. That way there is more fruit in autumn.
99891.m: Bees in the orchard make for a good harvest.

99892.q: Why do cherry trees blossom before they bear cherries?
99892.e: The cherries later grow from pollinated cherry blossoms. That is why the blossom comes first.
99892.m: Without blossoms there are no cherries.

99893.q: Where does pollen get stuck on a bee?
a: on the tips of its feelers
99893.e: Bees are covered in fine hairs. Lots of pollen grains stick to them.
99893.m: Pollen sticks to the bees' hairs.

99894.q: Which part of the flower takes up the pollen?
99894.e: The stigma is sticky. The pollen gets stuck there, and the flower is pollinated.
99894.m: The sticky stigma catches the pollen.

99895.q: Why are there often fewer cherries after a rainy spring?
a: Bees hardly fly in the rain.
No leaves grow in the rain.
99895.e: Bees have to fly while the cherry trees are in blossom. In rain and cold they stay in the hive, and many blossoms are not pollinated.
99895.m: Rain during blossom time can make the harvest smaller.

99896.q: What is the mother of all the bees in a colony called?
99896.e: Every bee colony has a queen. She lays all the eggs.
99896.m: The queen lays the eggs in the bee colony.

99897.q: What are the female bees that collect nectar called?
99897.e: The workers collect nectar and pollen, build honeycomb and look after the young.
99897.m: The workers do almost all the jobs in the bee colony.

99898.e: Male bees are called drones. They have no sting and do not collect nectar.

99899.q: How do bees show other bees the way to flowers?
99899.e: A collecting bee dances on the honeycomb in the hive. This tells the others the direction and distance of the flowers.
99899.m: Bees reveal with a dance where the flowers are.

99900.q: How many eyes does a honeybee have?
99900.e: The bee has two big compound eyes. On top of that there are three small simple eyes on the top of its head.

99901.q: Why does a honeybee often die when it stings a person?
99901.e: The sting has tiny barbs. It gets stuck in human skin and tears off.
99901.m: The honeybee's sting gets stuck in our skin.

99902.q: What does a bumblebee's body look like?
99902.e: Bumblebees have a fat, round body with lots of hairs. The fur keeps them warm.
99902.m: Bumblebees are round and have thick fur.

99903.q: When can bumblebees still fly while honeybees stay in the hive?
99903.e: Bumblebees warm themselves up with their flight muscles. That is why they fly even in cool temperatures.
99903.m: Bumblebees fly even in cool weather.

99904.q: Who in a bumblebee colony survives the winter?
99904.e: In autumn the bumblebee colony dies. Only young queens survive the winter and start a new colony in spring.
99904.m: Only the young bumblebee queen survives the winter.

99905.q: Where do many bumblebees build their nest?
99905.e: Many bumblebees nest in old mouse holes or other hollows in the ground.
99905.m: Bumblebees often nest in holes in the ground.

99906.q: What noise do bumblebees make when they fly?
99906.e: The bumblebee's wings beat fast. This makes a deep buzzing sound.

99907.q: What do vegetable growers use bumblebees for in the greenhouse?
99907.e: Bumblebees shake the pollen out of tomato flowers with vibrations. This produces more tomatoes.
99907.m: Bumblebees pollinate the tomatoes in the greenhouse.

99908.q: Which group of animals do bumblebees belong to?
99908.e: Bumblebees are a group of bees. Like other bees, they collect nectar and pollen.

99909.q: How big is a bumblebee colony compared with a honeybee colony?
99909.e: A bumblebee colony usually has only a few hundred animals. A honeybee colony is many times bigger.
99909.m: Bumblebee colonies are much smaller than honeybee colonies.

99910.q: Roughly how many kinds of wild bee live in Switzerland?
99910.e: More than 600 kinds of wild bee are known in Switzerland. Many of them have become rare.
99910.m: About 600 kinds of wild bee live in Switzerland.

99911.q: How do most wild bees live?
99911.e: Most wild bees live alone. Each female builds her own nest.

99912.q: Where do many wild bees nest?
99912.e: Many kinds of wild bee dig their nests in the ground. They like open, sandy spots.
99912.m: Many wild bees nest in the ground.

99913.q: Which wild bee likes to nest in hollow plant stems?
99913.e: The red mason bee nests in hollow stems, cracks and small holes. That is why it likes moving into a bee hotel.
99913.m: The mason bee nests in cracks and tubes.

99914.q: Which food do we get from honeybees but not from wild bees?
99914.e: Wild bees also collect nectar and pollen. But they do not store honey that a beekeeper can harvest.
99914.m: Wild bees do not produce honey for the beekeeper.

99915.q: How can you help wild bees in the garden?
99915.e: Wild bees need lots of different flowers. A wild flower meadow gives them food.

99916.q: Which wild bee likes to dig its nest in sandy ground?
99916.e: Mining bees dig small tunnels in sandy ground. You often see little heaps of earth in front of the entrance.
99916.m: Mining bees dig their nests in the ground.

99917.q: Which wild bee collects plant hairs for its nest?
99917.e: The wool carder bee scrapes fine hairs off plants. It uses them to line its nest.
99917.m: The wool carder bee lines its nest with plant hairs.

99918.q: Which big wild bee is bluish black and gnaws tunnels into dead wood?
99918.e: The violet carpenter bee is one of the biggest bees in Europe. It nests in rotten wood.
99918.m: The carpenter bee gnaws its nest into dead wood.

99919.q: What do butterflies need in the morning before they can fly well?
99919.e: Butterflies warm themselves up in the sun. They often sit with their wings open to do this.
99919.m: Butterflies first soak up warmth from the sun.

99920.q: What hatches from a butterfly's egg?
99920.e: A caterpillar hatches from the egg. It eats a lot and grows fast.
99920.m: A caterpillar hatches from a butterfly egg.

99921.q: What does the caterpillar do before it becomes a butterfly?
99921.e: The caterpillar turns into a pupa. Inside the pupa it changes into a butterfly.
99921.m: Inside the pupa the caterpillar becomes a butterfly.

99922.q: Which butterfly is bright yellow and flies very early in spring?
99922.e: The brimstone spends the winter as an adult butterfly. On warm days in February or March it is already flying.
99922.m: The yellow brimstone flies very early in the year.

99923.q: Which butterfly has big eyespots on its wings?
99923.e: The peacock butterfly has four colourful spots that look like eyes. They startle birds.
99923.m: The peacock butterfly startles enemies with eyespots.

99924.q: What lies like fine dust on butterfly wings?
99924.e: Butterfly wings are covered in tiny scales. That is why you should not touch them.

99925.q: Which white butterfly likes to lay its eggs on cabbage plants?
99925.e: The caterpillars of the cabbage white eat cabbage leaves. That is why the butterfly lays its eggs on cabbage.
99925.m: The cabbage white lays its eggs on cabbage.

99926.q: What do butterflies use to taste whether a leaf is good?
99926.e: Butterflies have taste cells on their feet. This is how they test plants.

99927.q: Which butterfly has black and yellow wings with long tails at the back?
99927.e: The swallowtail has two long tails at the back, like the tail of a swallow.
99927.m: The swallowtail has tailed hind wings.

99928.q: Which animal do many hoverflies look like?
99928.e: Many hoverflies are striped yellow and black like wasps. This protects them from birds.

99929.e: Hoverflies have no sting. They only look dangerous.

99930.q: What are hoverflies especially good at in the air?
a: Flying across the sea without a break
99930.e: Hoverflies beat their wings very fast. This lets them stand almost still in the air.
99930.m: Hoverflies can stand still in the air.

99931.q: What do the larvae of many hoverflies eat?
99931.e: Many hoverfly larvae eat hundreds of aphids. That is why they are useful in the garden.

99932.q: How many wings does a hoverfly have?
99932.e: Hoverflies are flies. Flies have only one pair of wings, wasps have two pairs.

99933.q: Which group of animals do hoverflies belong to?
99933.e: Despite their stripes, hoverflies are true flies. You can tell by their short feelers.

99934.e: Adult hoverflies visit flowers. While doing so they pollinate the plants.
99934.m: Adult hoverflies live on nectar and pollen.

99935.q: Why are hoverflies striped like wasps?
99935.e: Birds avoid wasps because they sting. That is why they often leave the harmless hoverflies alone too.
99935.m: The wasp colours protect the hoverfly.

99936.q: What do the flowers of plants whose pollen is carried by the wind often look like?
99936.e: Plants that have the wind as a helper do not need to attract insects. That is why such flowers are inconspicuous.

99937.q: Which colour can bees not see?
99937.e: Bees see red only as a dark, almost black colour. That is why red flowers hardly catch their eye.

99938.q: Which light can bees see but we cannot?
99938.e: Bees see ultraviolet light. That is why flowers look different to them than to us.

99939.q: A yellow spot in a horse chestnut flower later turns red. What does that show?
a: There is no more nectar here.
There is especially a lot of nectar here.
99939.e: Young flowers have yellow spots and lots of nectar. Later the spot turns red, and bees prefer to fly to fresh flowers.
99939.m: In the horse chestnut, the colour of the spot shows whether there is nectar.

99940.q: Which flower colour do night-flying moths find best?
99940.e: In the twilight, white flowers stand out best. That is why moths find them easily.
99940.m: White flowers glow in the twilight.

99941.q: Which flower colours do bees especially like?
99941.e: Bees see blue and yellow very well. That is why they often fly to such flowers.
99941.m: Bees like flying to blue and yellow flowers.

99942.q: What colour is the centre of a daisy?
99942.e: The daisy has white petals on the outside and a yellow centre. The yellow centre attracts insects.
99942.m: The daisy has a yellow centre.

99943.q: Which creatures in America like flying to red flowers?
99943.e: Hummingbirds see red very well and drink nectar. Many red flowers in America are visited by them.
99943.m: Hummingbirds like flying to red flowers.

99944.q: How does a bumblebee notice that a flower has just been visited?
a: by the colour of the root
99944.e: Bumblebees leave a faint scent on the flower when they visit. Other bumblebees smell it and fly on.
99944.m: Bumblebees recognise visited flowers by their scent.

99945.q: What do bees use to smell the scent of flowers?
99945.e: The bee has lots of smell cells on its feelers. With them it can smell flowers very well.

99946.q: When do many flowers for moths smell strongest?
99946.e: Many flowers visited by moths only smell strongly in the evening. That is when these moths are out and about.
99946.m: Flowers for moths smell in the evening.

99947.q: Which creatures does a flower that stinks of rotten meat attract?
99947.e: Some flowers smell of rotten meat. This attracts flies, which pollinate them.

99948.q: Which climbing plant with long flower tubes attracts moths with its scent?
99948.e: Honeysuckle has long, narrow flower tubes. Moths get the nectar out with their long tongues.
99948.m: Honeysuckle attracts moths with its scent.

99949.q: What does a flower's scent tell insects?
99949.e: The scent says: there is nectar or pollen here. Insects learn such scents quickly.
99949.m: The scent of a flower reveals that there is food.

99950.q: In what weather can you usually smell flower scent especially well?
99950.e: Warmth makes the scent substances rise into the air more easily. That is why a garden smells strong on warm days.
99950.m: Flowers smell stronger in warm weather.

99951.q: How do bees remember good flowers?
a: by the weight of the leaves
by the length of the root
99951.e: Bees learn fast. They remember the scent and colour of flowers with lots of nectar.
99951.m: Bees remember the scent and colour of good flowers.

99952.q: Who lives in an insect hotel?
99952.e: In an insect hotel, wild bees and other insects find tubes and holes to lay their eggs in.
99952.m: Wild bees and other insects live in the insect hotel.

99953.q: Which way should an insect hotel face?
99953.e: Wild bees like it warm. A spot in the sun, ideally facing south, is perfect.
99953.m: An insect hotel belongs in a sunny spot.

99954.q: What is often put into an insect hotel?
99954.e: Hollow bamboo or reed tubes are ideal nesting tubes for wild bees.
99954.m: Hollow tubes are good homes for wild bees.

99955.q: What should the roof of an insect hotel protect against?
99955.e: The inside should stay dry. A small roof keeps the rain off.
99955.m: A roof keeps the insect hotel dry.

99956.q: What is needed near an insect hotel?
99956.e: Wild bees need food. Without flowers nearby, the hotel stays empty.
99956.m: An insect hotel needs flowers nearby.

99957.q: Into which material do you drill holes for an insect hotel?
99957.e: Good nesting holes are drilled into dry hardwood, for example beech or oak.
99957.m: Nesting holes are drilled into hardwood.

99958.q: Which bees especially like moving into an insect hotel?
99958.e: Mason bees nest in tubes and holes. That is why you often find them in an insect hotel.
99958.m: Mason bees like moving into the insect hotel.

99959.q: What should the inside of the holes in an insect hotel be like?
99959.e: Splinters can injure the delicate wings. That is why the holes should be smooth.
99959.m: Smooth holes protect the bees' wings.

99960.q: What do bees make honey from?
99960.e: Bees suck up nectar and bring it to the hive. There it is turned into honey.

99961.q: What is a person who keeps bees called?
99961.e: The beekeeper looks after their bee colonies and harvests the honey.

a: as a store for the winter
99962.e: In winter there are no flowers. The bees then eat their store of honey.
99962.m: Honey is the bees' winter store.

99963.q: Where do bees store the honey?
99963.e: The bees fill the honey into the cells of the honeycomb and seal them with wax.

99964.q: What often happens to runny honey after a while?
99964.e: Honey contains a lot of sugar. Over time the sugar forms crystals and the honey sets.

99965.q: What do bees make dark forest honey from?
99965.e: Aphids give off a sweet juice called honeydew. Bees collect it and make forest honey from it.
99965.m: Forest honey is made from honeydew.

99966.q: Which device does the beekeeper use to get the honey out of the combs?
99966.e: In the honey extractor the combs spin fast. This flings the honey out.
99966.m: The beekeeper spins the honey out of the combs.

99967.e: Honey consists mostly of sugar. That is why it tastes sweet.

99968.q: How many spots does the best-known ladybird in our country have?
99968.e: The seven-spot ladybird is very well known here. It has red wing cases with seven black spots.
99968.m: The best-known ladybird has seven spots.

99969.q: Do the spots show a ladybird's age?
99969.e: The number of spots depends on the species. It does not change with age.
99969.m: The spots show the species, not the age.

99970.q: What does a ladybird do when in danger?
a: It gives off a yellow juice
99970.e: The ladybird gives off a yellow, bitter juice from its legs. Enemies do not like the taste.
99970.m: In danger, the ladybird gives off a bitter juice.

99971.q: What does the ladybird larva eat?
99971.e: The larvae eat aphids too, and a great many of them. They look quite different from the beetles.

99972.q: How do ladybirds often spend the winter?
99972.e: In autumn, ladybirds look for sheltered places such as cracks or leaves. Often lots of them lie together.
99972.m: Ladybirds like spending the winter in groups.

99973.q: What do many people see the ladybird as?
a: as a sign of bad luck
99973.e: The ladybird is a popular lucky charm. In German it is even called the lucky beetle.
99973.m: The ladybird is seen as a lucky charm.

99974.e: The red colour warns birds: I don't taste good. That is why they rarely eat it.

99975.q: What shape are the cells of a honeycomb?
99975.e: The honeycomb cells have six corners. That way they fit next to each other without gaps.

99976.q: What is the opening that bees fly through into the hive called?
99976.e: The bees fly in and out through the entrance hole. Guard bees keep watch there.
99976.m: Bees fly into the hive through the entrance hole.

99977.q: What does the beekeeper use to calm the bees?
99977.e: Smoke makes the bees calmer. The beekeeper uses a smoker for this.
99977.m: The beekeeper calms the bees with smoke.

99978.q: What does the beekeeper wear for protection against stings?
99978.e: A beekeeper's veil protects the face and neck from bee stings.
99978.m: The beekeeper protects their face with a veil.

99979.q: How many queens normally live in a beehive?
99979.e: A bee colony normally has only one queen.
99979.m: A bee colony has one queen.

99980.q: How do bees keep warm in winter?
99980.e: In winter the bees huddle closely together. In this winter cluster they shiver their muscles and make warmth.
99980.m: In winter bees keep warm in a cluster.

99981.q: Roughly how many bees live in a strong bee colony in summer?
99981.e: In summer about 40,000 to 60,000 bees live in a strong colony.
99981.m: A strong bee colony has tens of thousands of bees in summer.

100072.q: What should you do a lot of when you have a fever?
100072.e: When you have a fever, you sweat and lose a lot of water. That is why it is important to drink a lot.
100072.m: If you have a fever, drink plenty.

100073.q: How does your forehead often feel when you have a fever?
100073.e: With a fever, your whole body is warmer than usual. That is why your forehead often feels hot.
100073.m: With a fever, your forehead often feels hot.

100074.q: What do you often feel when a fever is rising?
a: You have to laugh a lot.
100074.e: When a fever rises, the body wants to get warmer. That is why you feel cold and shiver; this is called the chills.
100074.m: When a fever rises, you often feel cold and shiver.

100075.q: What usually happens when a fever goes down again?
100075.e: When a fever goes down, the body gives off heat. You often sweat a lot.
100075.m: When a fever goes down, you often sweat.

100076.q: When should you take a child with a fever to the doctor?
100076.e: A fever on its own is often not serious. But if a child seems very ill, is not drinking, or a very young baby has a fever, you should see a doctor.
100076.m: If a child seems very ill, you go to the doctor.

100077.q: What can an adult give a child with a high fever to bring it down?
100077.e: Fever medicine lowers the fever, and you feel better. The right amount is written in the leaflet or the doctor tells you.
100077.m: Fever medicine can bring down a high fever.

100078.q: What do you measure a fever with?
100078.e: A thermometer measures how warm the body is. That way you know whether someone has a fever.
100078.m: You measure a fever with a thermometer.

100079.q: In which unit does a thermometer in Switzerland show your temperature?
100079.e: In Switzerland, temperatures are measured in degrees Celsius. The unit is named after the Swede Anders Celsius.
100079.m: Temperature is measured in degrees Celsius.

100080.q: What does a digital thermometer often do when it has finished measuring?
100080.e: Digital thermometers beep when the measurement is finished. Then you can read the number.
100080.m: A digital thermometer beeps when it has finished.

100081.q: What does a digital thermometer need to work?
100081.e: A digital thermometer has a small display and a sensor. Both run on electricity from a small battery.
100081.m: A digital thermometer runs on a battery.

100082.q: Where can you quickly measure a child's temperature with a special thermometer?
100082.e: There are ear thermometers. You hold one in the ear for a moment, and after a few seconds it shows the temperature.
100082.m: An ear thermometer measures in the ear.

100083.q: What should you do after using a thermometer?
100083.e: Germs can stick to the thermometer. That is why you clean it after use, for example with soap and water or disinfectant.

100084.q: How do many forehead thermometers measure temperature?
100084.e: Many forehead thermometers measure the heat given off by the skin. You do not have to touch the forehead, or only briefly.
100084.m: A forehead thermometer measures the warmth of the skin.

100085.q: What do you often have when you have a cold?
100085.e: With a cold, your nose often runs or gets blocked. Sometimes you also have a cough and a sore throat.
100085.m: With a cold, you often have a runny nose.

100086.e: A cold is caused by viruses. There are lots of different cold viruses.

100087.q: In which season are colds especially common?
100087.e: In winter, people are more often together in warm rooms. Cold viruses can spread easily there.
100087.m: Lots of people catch colds in winter.

100088.q: Where is the best place to sneeze so that you do not infect anyone?
a: Into the crook of your elbow
100088.e: If you sneeze into the crook of your elbow, you spread fewer germs. Otherwise your hands would carry the viruses everywhere.
100088.m: Sneeze and cough into the crook of your elbow.

100089.q: What helps you to catch fewer illnesses?
100089.e: Viruses often stick to your hands. If you wash your hands regularly with soap, you catch fewer illnesses.
100089.m: Washing your hands protects against infection.

100090.q: Roughly how long does a cold last?
100090.e: A cold usually lasts about a week. After that you are healthy again.
100090.m: A cold usually lasts about a week.

100091.q: Where do you throw a used paper tissue?
100091.e: A used tissue contains lots of viruses. That is why you throw it straight in the bin.
100091.m: Used tissues go in the bin.

100092.q: Which word describes a nose that is completely closed up?
100092.e: With a cold, the skin inside your nose swells. Then your nose is blocked and you breathe through your mouth.
100092.m: With a cold, your nose is often blocked.

100093.q: What can help to clear a blocked nose?
100093.e: A saltwater nasal spray moistens the nose and loosens the mucus. Afterwards you can breathe better.
100093.m: Saltwater nasal spray makes your nose moist and clear.

100094.q: When does a sore throat hurt most?
100094.e: With a sore throat, your throat is inflamed. When you swallow, food rubs against it, so that is when it hurts most.
100094.m: You feel a sore throat mainly when swallowing.

100095.q: What is often red and swollen when you have a sore throat?
100095.e: The tonsils are at the back of the throat. When they are inflamed, they become red and swollen.
100095.m: With a sore throat, the tonsils are often red.

100096.q: What often feels good when you have a sore throat?
100096.e: Warm tea with honey soothes the throat. Spicy or hard food irritates it.
100096.m: Warm tea with honey is good for your throat.

100097.q: What can you suck when you have a sore throat?
100097.e: Throat sweets make you produce more spit. That keeps your throat moist and eases the scratchiness.
100097.m: Throat sweets can ease a scratchy throat.

100098.q: Where is a compress sometimes put when you have a sore throat?
100098.e: A throat compress is a cloth that you wrap around your neck. Many people find it soothing when they have a sore throat.
100098.m: A throat compress goes around the neck.

100099.q: What can happen to your voice when your throat is inflamed?
100099.e: When your throat is inflamed, your vocal cords can also be irritated. Then your voice sounds hoarse.
100099.m: With a sore throat, your voice often becomes hoarse.

100100.q: What do people often gargle with when they have a sore throat?
100100.e: You take a little salt water into your mouth and gargle with it. Then you spit it out again.
100100.m: Some people gargle with salt water for a sore throat.

100101.q: Who looks into your throat when you have a sore throat?
100101.e: The doctor looks into your throat with a light. That way they can see how inflamed your throat is.
100101.m: The doctor looks into your throat with a light.

100102.q: What do you often have with a tummy bug?
100102.e: With a tummy bug, the stomach and gut are inflamed. You often have diarrhoea and are sick.
100102.m: With a tummy bug, you often have diarrhoea.

100103.q: What is most important when you have a tummy bug?
100103.e: Being sick and having diarrhoea makes the body lose a lot of water. That is why you need to drink small sips often.
100103.m: With a tummy bug, you should drink a lot.

100104.q: Which body parts are ill when you have a tummy bug?
100104.e: A tummy bug is an inflammation of the stomach and gut. It has nothing to do with real flu.
100104.m: With a tummy bug, the stomach and gut are ill.

100105.q: Which food is easy on the stomach when you have a tummy bug?
100105.e: Rusks are dry and light. Greasy and sweet food, on the other hand, is hard on the tummy.
100105.m: With a tummy bug, you eat light things like rusks.

100106.q: Why must you wash your hands well after a tummy bug?
100106.e: The germs that cause a tummy bug spread very easily. Washing your hands protects the others in your family.
100106.m: A tummy bug is very contagious.

100107.e: A tummy bug comes from tiny germs that you cannot see. They easily spread from person to person.
100107.m: A tummy bug comes from tiny germs.

100108.q: What is the best way to drink when you have a tummy bug?
100108.e: A poorly stomach cannot cope well with large amounts. Small sips are more likely to stay down.
100108.m: With a tummy bug, you drink in small sips.

100109.q: How long does a tummy bug usually last?
100109.e: A tummy bug is usually over after a few days. After that, your tummy still needs a little care.
100109.m: A tummy bug usually only lasts a few days.

100110.q: Who should give a child medicine?
100110.e: Medicines can do harm if you take the wrong amount. That is why an adult always gives them.

100111.q: Where do you buy medicines in Switzerland?
100111.e: Medicines are sold at the chemist's (pharmacy). The pharmacist gives advice.
100111.m: You buy medicines at the chemist's.

100114.q: What does the doctor write so that you can get a certain medicine?
100114.e: Some medicines are only available with a prescription from the doctor. You take the prescription to the pharmacy.
100114.m: For some medicines you need a prescription.

100115.q: Which germs do antibiotics help against?
100115.e: Antibiotics kill bacteria or slow down their growth. They do not help against viruses, for example with a cold.

100116.q: In what form do medicines you swallow often come?
100116.e: Many medicines come as tablets, capsules or syrup. You swallow them with a little water.
100116.m: Many medicines are swallowed as tablets.

100117.q: What should you do if a medicine is past its expiry date?
a: Take it back to the pharmacy
100117.e: Out-of-date medicines may no longer work properly. In Switzerland, you can hand them in at the pharmacy.
100117.m: Old medicines go back to the pharmacy.

100118.q: What do you take cough syrup for?
100118.e: Cough syrup is a liquid medicine. It is meant to ease a cough.
100118.m: Cough syrup helps with a cough.

100119.q: What do you use to measure out cough syrup?
100119.e: Many cough syrups come with a measuring spoon or cup. That way you take exactly the right amount.
100119.m: You measure cough syrup with a measuring spoon.

100120.q: What form does cough syrup have?
100120.e: Syrup is thick and runny and often sweet. That is why it is easy to swallow.

100121.q: Which cough remedy is often made at home from onions and sugar?
100121.e: For onion syrup, you chop onions finely and add sugar or honey. It is an old home remedy for coughs.
100121.m: Onion syrup is an old home remedy for coughs.

100122.q: Which plant is often in cough syrup for children?
100122.e: Many children's cough syrups contain an extract from ivy leaves. It is meant to loosen mucus.

100123.q: What should you do with the measuring spoon after the cough syrup?
100123.e: Syrup is sticky, and germs stay on the spoon. That is why you wash the measuring spoon after every use.
100123.m: Wash the measuring spoon after use.

100124.q: Why must you not drink cough syrup like a sweet treat?
100124.e: Cough syrup often tastes sweet, but it is a medicine. Too much of it can be harmful.
100124.m: Cough syrup is a medicine, not a sweet.

100125.q: Which sweet ingredient is in many home remedies for coughs?
100125.e: Honey forms a film over the throat and soothes it. But babies under one year old must not have honey.
100125.m: Honey is a popular home remedy for coughs.

100126.e: With bed rest, you stay in bed and take it easy. That way the body can build up strength.
100126.m: With bed rest, you stay in bed and rest.

100127.q: Why does sleep help you get better?
100127.e: When you sleep, the body saves energy. It needs this energy to fight the illness.
100127.m: The body recovers while you sleep.

100128.q: What should you not do when you have a fever?
100128.e: Sport is too tiring for the body when you have a fever. Only when you are healthy again can you do sport again.
100128.m: No sport when you have a fever.

100129.q: What do you do often during bed rest so that fresh air gets into the room?
100129.e: Fresh air is good for people who are ill. You open the window for a short time and keep warmly covered.
100129.m: Air a sickroom briefly and often.

100130.q: What is a quiet activity during bed rest?
100130.e: During bed rest you should not tire yourself out. An audiobook or a book are quiet activities.
100130.m: During bed rest you only do quiet things.

100131.q: Where should an ill child with a fever stay?
100131.e: With a fever, you need rest. Also, you can infect others, so you stay at home.
100131.m: With a fever, you stay at home.

100132.q: What is best to have next to the bed during bed rest?
100132.e: People who are ill should drink a lot. A glass of water or tea next to the bed reminds them.
100132.m: Keep something to drink next to a sickbed.

100133.q: What do you do during bed rest if your pyjamas are wet from sweating?
a: Put a winter coat on over them
100133.e: Wet clothes cool the body down and are uncomfortable. That is why you put on dry pyjamas after sweating.
100133.m: After sweating, you put on dry clothes.

100134.q: Which tea do people often drink for tummy ache?
100134.e: Camomile tea soothes the tummy. It is one of the best-known home remedies.

100135.q: Which tea do people often drink for a sore throat?
100135.e: Sage has been used for sore throats for a long time. You drink it as tea or gargle with it.
100135.m: Sage tea is often drunk for a sore throat.

100136.q: Which tea tastes fresh and cooling?
100136.e: Peppermint contains menthol. That is why the tea feels fresh and cool in your mouth.

100137.q: What is herbal tea made from?
100137.e: For herbal tea, you use dried leaves or flowers from plants. You pour hot water over them.
100137.m: Herbal tea is made from dried plants.

100138.q: Which tea is often given to small children for wind?
100138.e: Fennel soothes the tummy and helps against wind. Fennel tea is mild, so it is also suitable for children.

100139.q: Which part of the camomile plant is used to make tea?
100139.e: For camomile tea, you use the dried flowers. They are white with yellow centres.
100139.m: Camomile tea is made from the flowers.

100140.q: What must you be careful about when drinking freshly made tea?
100140.e: Tea is made with boiling water. That is why you let it cool down a little before you drink it.
100140.m: Let fresh tea cool down a little.

100141.q: Which tea do people often drink when they have a cold and a fever?
100141.e: Lime blossom tea is an old home remedy for colds. It is drunk warm.
100141.m: Lime blossom tea is a home remedy for colds.

100142.q: Roughly how long do you let herbal tea brew?
100142.e: The herbs need a few minutes in the hot water. Then the tea releases its flavour and its active ingredients.
100142.m: Let herbal tea brew for a few minutes.

100143.q: What do you see on the skin with chickenpox?
100143.e: With chickenpox, lots of small red spots and blisters form on the skin. They are very itchy.

100144.q: Why should you not scratch chickenpox blisters open?
a: You will then never be ill again
100144.e: Scratched blisters can become infected. Afterwards small scars are sometimes left.

100145.q: How often do people usually get chickenpox?
100145.e: Anyone who has had chickenpox is usually protected afterwards. That is why you normally only get it once.
100145.m: You usually only get chickenpox once.

100146.e: Chickenpox viruses fly through the air when people breathe and talk. That is why they spread very easily.

100147.e: Chickenpox is a typical childhood illness. Most people get it as children.

100148.e: There is a vaccination against chickenpox. It protects you from getting ill.

100149.q: What can help against the itching with chickenpox?
100149.e: A cooling lotion from the pharmacy soothes itchy skin. Warmth and scratchy wool often make the itching worse.
100149.m: A cooling lotion eases the itching.

100150.q: What do chickenpox blisters form after a few days?
100150.e: The blisters dry up after a few days. Then a scab forms, which later falls off.
100150.m: Chickenpox blisters dry up into scabs.

100151.q: Where do you put a calf compress?
100151.e: The calf is the back of the lower leg. You wrap damp cloths around it.
100151.m: A calf compress goes around the lower legs.

100152.q: What does a calf compress help against?
100152.e: Calf compresses can bring a high fever down a little. The damp cloth absorbs heat from the body.
100152.m: Calf compresses can lower a fever.

100153.q: What should the water for a calf compress be like?
100153.e: For calf compresses, you use water that is a little cooler than the body. Ice-cold water would be too unpleasant.
100153.m: Use lukewarm to cool water for calf compresses.

100154.q: When should you not use calf compresses?
a: When you are lying in bed
100154.e: When your feet are cold or you are shivering, the body wants to keep its warmth. Then you should not cool it down even more.
100154.m: No calf compresses when your feet are cold.

100155.q: What do you need for a calf compress?
100155.e: You dip a cloth in water, wring it out and wrap it around the calf. A dry cloth goes on top.
100155.m: For a calf compress you need cloths and water.

100156.q: What do you put over the wet cloth of a calf compress?
100156.e: A dry cloth goes over the damp cloth. That keeps the bed dry, and you take the compress off again after a few minutes.
100156.m: A dry cloth goes over the wet cloth.

100157.q: What do you do with the cloth before you put it around the calf?
100157.e: The cloth should be damp but not dripping wet. That is why you wring it out well first.
100157.m: Wring out the wet cloth before wrapping it.

100158.q: What effect does a calf compress have on the body?
100158.e: The water in the cloth evaporates and takes heat from the skin with it. That cools the body down.
100158.m: A calf compress cools the body.

100159.q: Who looks after children who are ill?
100159.e: A children's doctor specialises in children and young people. They know a lot about childhood illnesses.
100159.m: The children's doctor looks after ill children.

100160.q: What does the children's doctor use to listen to your heart and lungs?
100160.e: A stethoscope has two earpieces and a round chest piece. With it, the doctor listens to your heart and breathing.
100160.m: The doctor listens to your heart and lungs with a stethoscope.

100161.q: What is the technical term for children's medicine?
100161.e: Children's medicine is called paediatrics. A children's doctor is therefore a paediatrician.

100162.q: What do you get at the children's doctor to protect you against illnesses?
100162.e: You get vaccinations at the children's doctor. They protect against dangerous illnesses.
100162.m: You get vaccinations at the children's doctor.

100163.q: Where does the children's doctor look with a small light when you have earache?
100163.e: The doctor has a small ear scope with a light. With it, they can see deep into the ear as far as the eardrum.
100163.m: The doctor looks into the ear with a small light.

100164.q: What is often measured at a check-up with the children's doctor?
100164.e: At check-ups, the children's doctor measures height and weight. That way they can see whether a child is growing well.
100164.m: The children's doctor measures how tall a child is.

100165.q: What do you usually do before going to the children's doctor?
100165.e: Usually you first phone the children's doctor. That way you get an appointment.
100165.m: First make an appointment with the children's doctor.

100166.q: What is the room where you have to wait at the doctor's called?
100166.e: Before you go into the treatment room, you wait in the waiting room. There are often books and toys there.
100166.m: At the doctor's, you wait in the waiting room.

100167.q: Where do you go if a child suddenly becomes very ill at night?
100167.e: At night, the children's doctor's surgery is usually closed. In an emergency, you go to hospital or call the emergency number 144.
100167.m: In an emergency at night, the hospital helps.

100168.q: At what temperature does water boil in a saucepan at the seaside?
100168.e: At sea level, water boils at 100 degrees Celsius. Then big bubbles rise.
100168.m: At the seaside water boils at 100 degrees.

100169.q: What rises in the saucepan when the water boils?
100169.e: When it boils, water at the bottom turns into steam. The steam rises as bubbles.
100169.m: Boiling water makes bubbles of steam.

100170.q: In the mountains, does water boil at more or less than 100 degrees?
100170.e: In the mountains less air presses on the water. That is why it boils below 100 degrees, and pasta takes longer to cook.
100170.m: On a high mountain water boils below 100 degrees.

100171.q: Why do saucepans often have plastic handles?
a: They do not get as hot.
100171.e: Plastic conducts heat badly. So you can touch the handles without burning yourself so quickly.
100171.m: Plastic handles do not get as hot.

100172.q: What material are many saucepans made of?
100172.e: Many saucepans are made of metal, for example stainless steel. Metal conducts heat well to the food.

100173.q: What happens if you fill a saucepan too full of water and boil it?
100173.e: Boiling water bubbles upwards. If the pan is too full, it runs over the edge.
100173.m: A pan that is too full boils over.

100174.q: Why does the water at the top of the pan get warm too, even though only the bottom is hot?
a: The water at the top stays cold.
100174.e: At the bottom the water gets warm and rises. Cooler water sinks down, so everything warms up evenly.
100174.m: Warm water rises in the pan.

100175.q: What can you see above a pan of boiling water?
100175.e: The hot steam cools down in the air. Tiny water droplets form, which we see as a white cloud.
100175.m: Above boiling water you see a white cloud.

100176.q: Why do you put a lid on the pan when cooking?
100176.e: The lid keeps the heat in the pan. That is why the water gets hot faster and starts to boil sooner.
100176.m: With a lid, water boils faster.

100177.q: What do you save if you cook with a lid?
100177.e: With a lid, less heat is lost. That is why you need less energy to cook.
100177.m: Cooking with a lid saves energy.

100178.q: What collects on the inside of the lid?
100178.e: The steam meets the cooler lid. There it turns back into water and forms drops.
100178.m: On the lid, steam turns back into water.

100179.q: Why is a metal lid hot after cooking?
a: The hot steam has heated it.
It was kept in the fridge.
100179.e: The steam from the pan gives its heat to the lid. That is why you only hold it by the handle or with an oven glove.
100179.m: A metal lid gets hot from the steam.

100180.q: How should you lift a lid off a hot pan?
100180.e: There is hot steam under the lid. If you lift it away from your body, the steam does not rush into your face.
100180.m: Lift a lid away from your body.

100181.q: Why do some lids have a small hole?
a: So that light can get in
So that flies can get in
100181.e: Some steam can escape through the small hole. That way the lid rattles less and things do not boil over so easily.
100181.m: Steam escapes through the hole in the lid.

100182.q: What is a glass lid useful for?
a: You can see into the pan.
100182.e: You can see the food through glass without lifting the lid. That way the heat stays in the pan.
100182.m: You can look into the pan through a glass lid.

100183.q: What can you use to put out a fire in a frying pan with oil?
100183.e: A lid takes away the fire's air, and it goes out. Never pour water on burning oil: it turns to steam instantly and throws burning oil everywhere.
100183.m: Smother an oil fire with a lid, never with water.

100184.q: Where is the heating element in many kettles?
100184.e: The heating plate is at the bottom in the base. It passes its heat directly to the water.
100184.m: The heating element in a kettle is in the base.

100185.q: What does a kettle need to heat up?
100185.e: A kettle is plugged into a socket. The electricity makes the heating plate hot.

100186.q: What white layer builds up in a kettle over time?
100186.e: Tap water has lime dissolved in it. When it is heated, the lime settles as a white layer.
100186.m: Limescale builds up in a kettle.

100187.q: What can you use to remove limescale from a kettle?
100187.e: Vinegar is acidic and dissolves the limescale. Afterwards you rinse the kettle out well with water.

100188.q: Which is usually faster: boiling water in a kettle or in a pan on the cooker?
a: In a pan on the cooker
100188.e: In a kettle the heating element is right next to the water. So little heat is lost and the water boils quickly.
100188.m: Water boils quickly in a kettle.

100189.q: Why should you only fill the kettle with as much water as you need?
100189.e: Every litre of water takes energy to heat. If you only boil as much as you need, you save electricity.
100189.m: Boiling only as much water as you need saves electricity.

100190.q: Why does a kettle have a scale with lines on the outside?
a: To read how much water is in it
100190.e: The scale shows how much water is inside. That way you do not fill it too much or too little.
100190.m: You read the amount of water on the scale.

100191.q: Why must a kettle not be dipped into the sink?
100191.e: Water and electricity are dangerous together. That is why electrical appliances must never be dipped in water.
100191.m: Never dip electrical appliances in water.

100192.q: Why should you never switch a kettle on without water?
a: It would then need more water
It would never switch off again
100192.e: Without water, nothing takes up the heat from the heating plate. The appliance can overheat and break.
100192.m: Only switch a kettle on with water in it.

100193.q: What must you not put in the microwave?
